An air bubble in liquid accelerates upward due to a
buoyant force. If the bubble is in contact with a solid
surface, a friction force proportional to its velocity will
oppose the motion. When these 2 effects are balanced, the
bubble moves at a constant speed: the terminal velocity.

vertical ruler. A video camera was placed above the GC.
